AMH is one of the most talked-about fertility tests today — and the most misunderstood one too! 🧐

A normal AMH does not always guarantee fertility, 
and a low AMH does not mean pregnancy is impossible. 

AMH mainly reflects ovarian reserve, not egg quality, implantation, or overall reproductive health.

Understanding AMH in the right clinical context is important to avoid unnecessary fear, confusion, or false reassurance. 

Fertility is much more than a single number.🌸


🏥 Andheri and Juhu
Dr Ria Katwala Solanki

Do all fibroids need surgery? Know what you are in for.
Fibroids are the most common BENIGN growths found in women. Some can exist silently and cause no problem, while some can cause a range of symptoms like heavy menstrual bleeding, infertility, bloating, pain in the abdomen and so on. 
The location, size and symptoms of the fibroids determine the need for surgery.
We do not operate if:
Symptoms are mild and manageable.
You are close to menopause (fibroids often shrink afterward).
In these cases, we may just monitor them with periodic ultrasound exams.
We recommend surgery when- 
Very heavy menstrual bleeding.
Severe pelvic pain or pressure.
Infertility or pregnancy problems.
Very large fibroids.
Rapid growth.
Common surgeries include:
Myomectomy – removes fibroids but keeps the uterus.
Hysterectomy – removes the uterus (permanent solution).
These surgeries are performed via key-hole method- laparoscopy or robotic.
 Large fibroids are converted to smaller strips and removed via a 1cm cut in the abdomen. This method ensures more precision, faster recovery, less blood loss and better outcomes.
